title: One synthetic cellular automaton exposes the cost of forgetting state

plain_language.question: Can a state-aware invariant be strictly stronger than all fixed phase-blind two-label speed certificates for the same cellular automaton?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes, for the explicit synthetic three-state rule: every valid static certificate has attained east support one, but every finite nonempty spaceship has horizontal displacement zero.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Use a concrete fully model-linked example of information lost by state-blind abstraction, with an exact real-convex-hull comparison and a nontrivial oscillator.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is one synthetic three-state rule, not Life-like or empirical evidence; static support one does not mean an actual speed-one spaceship exists.

exact_statement_and_scope: For the specified synthetic three-state dead/r/l cellular automaton on the integer plane, every valid phase-blind fixed two-label local certificate has east-coordinate support exactly one, attained in the intersection of the two full Mathlib convexHull ℝ sets, not merely rational barycentric approximations. For the same actual evolve/iterate rule, potential p(r)=1,p(l)=0 proves that any finite nonempty initial configuration which recurs exactly as a translate after a natural number of steps has horizontal displacement zero, with arbitrary vertical displacement allowed. Thus horizontal velocity is zero for positive period. A finite nonempty two-cell oscillator is proved by full configuration equalities including the dead exterior. The strict separation is between this actual-rule stateful obstruction and this specified whole static-certificate family; it is not a new speed bound for a published or binary Life-like rule.
